correctness.rationale: The objects are 2-spaces in a 7-dimensional coefficient space; the four and only four rational projective members of a basis pair are [F], [G], [F+G], [F−G]. Degree d of F(X,1) leaves multiplicity 6−d at infinity; over the perfect field the affine derivative-gcd condition is exactly absence of repeated geometric roots. With a separately written replay I instead tested divisibility by squares of monic irreducibles of degree at most three and enumerated all 99,463 unique RREF subspaces, recovering 648 reduced projective forms and 10,005 all-smooth pencils. The common branch degree was independently counted from shared irreducibles through degree five and the common infinity flag; two distinct normalized forms cannot share an affine factor of degree six. All five base degrees and all five root profiles matched. Direct binomial substitution by all 24 projective matrices reproduced orbit multiplicities (1,1,43,395) at sizes (3,6,12,24), and independently verified all 440 catalogue rows, including representative members, joint statistics and sizes. The displayed example has common degree zero and orbit 24. Two independent rational sections vanishing at a rational point would have a nonzero combination with vanishing first jet, so no rational common base point occurs and evaluation gives exactly one vanishing pencil member per rational source point. The two jet constraints also prove the higher-dimensional bound for F3-linear systems. With no geometric base point, the map defined by the two sections pulls back O(1) to O(6) and its four rational fibers are the four reduced divisors. Characteristic three is odd, so reduced degree-six branch data give smooth genus-two double covers without any twist choice affecting the pencil census.
residual_risks: The census tests the four rational members, not all members after base extension. Only source-coordinate PGL2 acts on the subspaces; no count of twists or curve isomorphism classes follows.

evidence: Asgarli–Ghioca Theorem 1.3 assumes ambient dimension at least two and sufficiently large q. Zobernig Theorem 2 counts p-rank strata of M2 in characteristic three. Entin describes large-q section statistics. The split-quadric net and pencil constructions use F2 and bidegree-(2,3) forms.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The existence framework does not count F3 lines in the binary-sextic parameter space; moduli strata and asymptotic section statistics neither dominate the exact count nor yield the PGL2 orbit catalogue. The related split-quadric results are not blanket classifications of finite-field smooth linear systems.

value.rationale: This is a natural small-field example of avoiding singular rational members, at the standard sextic branch degree for genus two. For families rather than single curves the complete orbit catalogue is usable exact data. Its base-free stratum gives the count of corresponding degree-six maps up to choice of target coordinates before taking source orbits, with all four rational fibers reduced, and the other strata and root profiles distinguish substantive geometric and arithmetic behavior. The value is the exact incidence and symmetry classification, not the small field size, the dimension-bound observation, or computation alone.
residual_risks: The numerical invariant is specific to F3 and degree six and does not classify twists or general-field smooth systems.
